svg.text: §56's comparison of two 'holy lies', and the record of effects it leaves out
the Law-Book of Manu, as §56 quotes it
'A woman's mouth, a girl's breast, a child's prayer,
the smoke of a sacrifice are always pure'
what §56 reads in it: sexuality treated 'with reverence'
source: Jacolliot's French compilation, 1876
1 Corinthians 7:2, 9, as §56 quotes it
'To avoid fornication let every man have his own
wife … it is better to marry than to burn'
what §56 reads in it: sexuality as a concession
source: the Authorized Version
the verdict, §56
one code's lie serves life, the other's poisons it: 'to what end a lie is told'
a claim about effects on bodies; the passage supplies none
the record that would bear on it, and where it is
the same code, quoted by the same author weeks earlier: Twilight, 'Improvers of Mankind' §3
the Chandala may eat only garlic and onions; take water only 'from the entrances to swamps and holes
made by the feet of animals'; may not wash; may not be helped in childbirth; 'for clothing only rags
from corpses, for utensils broken pots'
the harvest, in the author's words: 'murderous epidemics, hideous venereal diseases'
the one effect on bodies in evidence, and it runs against Manu
what the comparison establishes: two codes sanctify different things; what it cannot: which lie serves life
